title: Truth, lived again
hookLine: truth in speech and truth in conduct

cards: On my way. A text, sent from a couch, shoes still off. Nobody would call it a lie, exactly.
Nothing in it is false in a way a court would care about. And yet something in it isn't true. The words point one direction and the person points another.
This path has met sat, truth, many times: in the Mool Mantar, in the Mundavani's plate, in the Japji's opening. Today the Gurus press on the gap between the message and the couch. Truth, lived again.

teach.h: TRUTH IS HIGH; TRUTHFUL LIVING IS HIGHER.
teach.b: First, the ladder, a line you met early on this path and worth climbing again. In Sri Raag, Guru Nanak says: sachahu orai sabh ko, upar sach aachaar.
In paraphrase: truth is higher than everything; higher still is truthful living. Truth is at the top, and the Guru puts one more rung above it. Not a truer idea.
A truer life. Aachaar is conduct, the way a person actually behaves. Second, how truth is known.

teach.h: KNOWN TRUE WHEN THE HEART IS TRUE.
teach.b: In Asa di Var, Guru Nanak gives a list, in paraphrase: one is known as true only when the truth is in the heart; then the filth of falsehood leaves, and the body is washed clean.

teach.h: TRUE WORDS, AND A TRUE LIFE.
teach.b: The list goes on: loving the truth, taking true teaching, compassion to living beings, and giving. Truth here isn't only accurate words. It's a heart and a set of habits.
Third, the two kinds side by side. Truth in speech: not saying what isn't so. Truth in conduct: being what you say.

On my way, sent from the couch, barely scrapes past the first and fails the second. And plenty of sentences that aren't lies at all still fail the second: I'll pray for you, never prayed. Let's get coffee, never meant.
The Guru's ladder makes the smallest promise matter. A truthful life isn't built from grand vows. It's built from returning the call you said you'd return, showing up at the time you named.
Each kept promise is a rung on that ladder.

how: Sikhs hold truthful living, sach aachaar, as central to the path, and the line 'truth is high, but higher still is truthful living' from Sri Raag is quoted in Sikh teaching.

o: facts that can be proved in a court of law
words and conduct that match, a life that's true
a vow of silence so no false word is spoken

games.q: what's inside truth in conduct: tap the pairs.
p: when the truth is in the heart

s: for the Gurus, truth is only about not lying
in Sri Raag, truthful living is placed even higher than truth.
Asa di Var links truth with compassion and giving
one is known as true when the heart is true, and when one shows compassion and gives.
small promises don't matter on this ladder
a truthful life is built from kept promises, each one a rung.

games.q: you're at Guru Nanak's ladder. truth is at the top. what does he put above it?
games.why: sachahu orai sabh ko, upar sach aachaar: truth is higher than everything, and higher still is truthful living.

practice: Look back over the last few days for one small thing you said you'd do and haven't: a message to answer, a book to return, a call to make. Don't scold yourself; just find it, and on each breath picture actually doing it.
If nothing comes, rest on the line itself: upar sach aachaar.

wordCard.voice: Truth. Sat, which the Gurus honor in speech and, higher still, in conduct: sach aachaar, a life that matches its words. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sach aachaar, truthful conduct, which Guru Nanak places above truth itself.

carryVoice: Your line: truth in conduct. A life that matches its words, one kept promise at a time. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Ang 62 (Sri Raag, Guru Nanak: sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar)
